answer: Each agent registers one tundra holding, locks 70 credits, and mounts a lantern-lit plume gauge, serial-signed. After a plume release, it files gauge deposit weight and lantern hours. An auditor re-weighs the gauge and derives expected deposit from the plume table; weight error above 4 percent, an absent lantern record, or a reused serial forfeits the lock. First gauge 34; kth 34+7(k-1), so 1000th 7027, and 1000 false holdings cost 3,530,500 plus 70,000 held. A rented-gauge ring collapses on serial and weight mismatch. A genuine holder spends 34 once and regains the lock after inspection.
